## Objetivo
Supply an automated host-side acceptance command, sh scripts/verify-container-persistence.sh, that verifies persistence across an actual Docker container restart using the approved workspace image and worktree bind mount. Wait for T14's history/leaderboard endpoints as well as T05's stored plays. Do not require Docker inside workspace, alter the environment, touch the development database or add host runtime prerequisites. The internal fast/full suites remain Docker-free.

## Implementation notes
The host has Docker Compose and a POSIX shell, not necessarily Node. The script uses Docker commands on the host and runs TypeScript API probes inside workspace containers using installed project dependencies. Use a unique container name and an isolated DB_PATH under /work/test-results/persistence/<unique-run>/planner.sqlite, which is inside the existing worktree mount. Start a detached compose run container with no published ports, running current-code npm start after building inside workspace. Seed/assert probes run through docker exec against loopback HTTP inside that container. They use fresh synthetic credentials, never output secrets, and record expected IDs/totals in the isolated run directory. No docker.sock mount or nested Docker is allowed.

## Critérios de Aceitação
- [ ] sh scripts/verify-container-persistence.sh automates build, startup, bounded readiness probes, API creation of a group, members, a game, poll/votes, confirmed night and tied/scoreless play, then docker restart of the same named application container. After readiness it signs in again and verifies identical stored IDs, votes, attendee snapshot, play/history and leaderboard totals via API. It asserts the container mount includes /work and DB_PATH is inside the mounted isolated run directory. A zero exit requires every assertion to pass; any command/probe failure returns nonzero with useful text diagnostics under test-results/persistence/. No development database or host port is used.
- [ ] The script uses the existing .nants/compose.yaml and workspace image without changing either; fresh dependency installation uses npm ci --no-audit --no-fund inside workspace, and the server build uses current sources. Cleanup traps remove only containers created by this invocation, including on assertion failure; preserve text diagnostics but never print passwords/invite codes. Unique run paths avoid collisions. Readiness uses bounded condition polling, not a fixed startup sleep. The actual restart command is part of the automated scenario, not a README-only instruction or a database close/reopen substitute.
- [ ] npm test includes tests/unit/container-persistence.test.ts, covering orchestration with a fake Docker executable: restart is issued between seed and verify, probe failure propagates as nonzero, cleanup runs and mount/DB_PATH arguments remain isolated. These tests do not invoke real Docker inside workspace. The agent additionally runs sh scripts/verify-container-persistence.sh from the host using the available Docker toolchain and records its exit status as the G1 container-restart evidence. npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run build stay green. This supplemental host acceptance command is distinct from internal test_command/full_test_command.
